title: Sitting Down

learn.summary: Posture matters only insofar as it keeps you alert and comfortable for the whole session: stable base, upright spine, relaxed everything else. A chair is completely legitimate; full lotus earns you nothing extra. The classic instruction is a posture that is both dignified and at ease.

do: Set up one dedicated spot (chair or cushion) today and do a 5-minute sit there before tomorrow night.

children.title: Posture Options

learn.summary: Four workable options: chair (feet flat, sit away from the backrest), cross-legged on a cushion (hips above knees), kneeling seiza with a bench, or lying down (highest sleep risk). Knee or back pain usually means your hips are too low; raise the cushion. Choose for sustainability over aesthetics.

do: Test two different postures for 5 minutes each this week and commit to the one you could hold for 20 minutes.

children.title: Eyes and Hands

learn.summary: Eyes closed increases inward focus but also drowsiness; the Zen alternative is eyes half-open with a soft downward gaze about a meter ahead. Hands simply rest on thighs or folded in the lap; the cosmic mudra is tradition, not requirement. If you keep dozing off, open your eyes; if you keep getting distracted, close them.

do: Do one sit eyes-closed and one eyes-half-open this week and note which kept you more alert.

children.title: Environment

learn.summary: You need less than you think: a spot with predictably few interruptions for the length of your sit. A consistent location builds a context cue that makes starting automatic, the same mechanism behind any habit anchor. Noise is workable (it becomes practice material later); interruption by other people mostly is not.

do: Tell the people you live with a specific 10-minute daily window when you are not to be interrupted, starting this week.

children.title: Timers and Length

learn.summary: Always use a timer so you stop negotiating with the clock mid-sit; a gentle bell beats a jarring alarm. Start at 5-10 minutes daily; MBSR assigns 45 minutes but that is with weekly teacher support, and daily consistency beats occasional heroics. Increase by about 5 minutes only when the current length feels routine for two straight weeks.

do: Set a recurring daily 10-minute timer with a bell sound today and use it for 7 consecutive days.

reflect: What does your mind offer you as a reason to skip sitting today? Write the excuse down without obeying or fighting it.
